To create a comprehensive codelist for a **wrist fracture**, we must include codes that describe fractures of the bones that make up the wrist. This includes the distal (lower end) of the radius and ulna, as well as the carpal bones (e.g., scaphoid, lunate). 

This codelist specifically includes:
* **Distal radius and ulna fractures** (e.g., Colles', Smith's, Barton's, Galeazzi, and radial/ulnar styloid fractures)
* **Carpal bone fractures** (e.g., scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum, pisiform, trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate)
* **Fracture-dislocations of the wrist** (e.g., radiocarpal, midcarpal, and carpometacarpal joints)
* **Surgical & Casting Procedure codes** specifically for wrist or scaphoid fractures (which indicate a recent, active wrist fracture)

*Note: Fractures strictly describing the metacarpals or phalanges (which occur in the hand and fingers) have been deliberately excluded to ensure accuracy.*

To create a comprehensive codelist for a **wrist fracture**, we must include codes that describe fractures of the bones that make up the wrist. This includes the distal (lower end) of the radius and ulna, as well as the carpal bones (e.g., scaphoid, lunate). 

This codelist specifically includes:
* **Distal radius and ulna fractures** (e.g., Colles', Smith's, Barton's, Galeazzi, and radial/ulnar styloid fractures)
* **Carpal bone fractures** (e.g., scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum, pisiform, trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate)
* **Fracture-dislocations of the wrist** (e.g., radiocarpal, midcarpal, and carpometacarpal joints)
* **Surgical & Casting Procedure codes** specifically for wrist or scaphoid fractures (which indicate a recent, active wrist fracture)

*Note: Fractures strictly describing the metacarpals or phalanges (which occur in the hand and fingers) have been deliberately excluded to ensure accuracy.*

To create a comprehensive codelist for a **wrist fracture**, we must include codes that describe fractures of the bones that make up the wrist. This includes the distal (lower end) of the radius and ulna, as well as the carpal bones (e.g., scaphoid, lunate). 

This codelist specifically includes:
* **Distal radius and ulna fractures** (e.g., Colles', Smith's, Barton's, Galeazzi, and radial/ulnar styloid fractures)
* **Carpal bone fractures** (e.g., scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum, pisiform, trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate)
* **Fracture-dislocations of the wrist** (e.g., radiocarpal, midcarpal, and carpometacarpal joints)
* **Surgical & Casting Procedure codes** specifically for wrist or scaphoid fractures (which indicate a recent, active wrist fracture)

*Note: Fractures strictly describing the metacarpals or phalanges (which occur in the hand and fingers) have been deliberately excluded to ensure accuracy.*

content.text:
To capture a "wrist fracture" in CPRD, you should include diagnostic codes for fractures of the distal forearm (distal radius and distal ulna), the carpal bones (scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum, pisiform, trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate), and specific fracture patterns of the wrist (Colles', Smith's, Barton's, Galeazzi, etc.). Codes for fracture-dislocations and subluxations of the carpal and radiocarpal joints are also included.
